rubric.why: An ion is distinguished by carrying an electrical charge.
rubric.description: States that an ion is a charged atom or group of atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the ion as charged.

rubric.why: An unpaired electron is the defining feature of a free radical.
rubric.description: States that a free radical contains one or more unpaired electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning unpaired electrons in a free radical.

modelAnswer: An ion is an atom or group of atoms that carries a positive or negative charge.
A free radical is an atom or group of atoms containing one or more unpaired electrons.

items.followUp: How many protons and neutrons are present in tritium, ³₁H?

rubric.why: Deuterium has atomic number 1, so its nucleus contains one proton.
rubric.description: Gives the number of protons in deuterium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that deuterium has one proton.

rubric.why: Deuterium has mass number 2 and atomic number 1, so it has 2 − 1 = 1 neutron.
rubric.description: Gives the number of neutrons in deuterium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that deuterium has one neutron.

modelAnswer: Deuterium is ²₁H, so its atomic number is 1 and its mass number is 2.
Number of neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 2 − 1 = 1.

rubric.why: A neutral magnesium atom has 12 electrons because its atomic number is 12.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating or correctly using the number of electrons in a neutral Mg atom.

rubric.why: This is the correct filling of the subshells for magnesium’s 12 electrons.
rubric.description: Gives the complete subshell electronic configuration of magnesium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct complete configuration.

modelAnswer: Magnesium has atomic number 12, so a neutral Mg atom has 12 electrons.
Filling the subshells in order gives: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s².
